asking: A person has to run runbook step 5 against the database and name the catalog row: SELECT slug, package_unit FROM ingredients WHERE package_unit IS NOT NULL AND package_unit NOT IN ('g','ml','pcs'). The telemetry pins the stage, the exception class, the source line and the release; the ingredient id is in the exception message, which is withheld from telemetry on purpose (HLD §8, #57), and reading catalog rows is F2. Two questions for whoever picks this up: (1) which row is it, and (2) is RATION_RESOLVE_PACKAGE_UNITS to stay on while that row is fixed, or to be turned off first to give the follower a working shopping list?
responder: on-call-responder agent (staged exercise run, started by a person)

diagnosis.summary: Every request to GET /api/plans/{plan_id}/shopping-list on release `dev` in `development` fails in the fourth pipeline stage, `shopping_list.convert_yield`, with `UnrecognisedUnitError` raised at backend/src/ration/domain/units.py:124 (`dimension_for`), called from domain/shopping.py:135 (`convert_to_raw`) via api/pipelines.py:62. The three stages before it complete on every trace inspected (load_catalog 40 items out, load_plan 27 out, expand_entries 114 out), so the failure is in the raw-weight conversion and not upstream of it.
diagnosis.mechanism_from_code: `convert_to_raw` only checks units when `resolve_units=True`, and pipelines.py passes `settings().resolve_package_units` (config.py:32, env `RATION_RESOLVE_PACKAGE_UNITS`, default false). The exception being raised at all is therefore evidence that the flag is ON in the running service. The flag's own comment says the check shipped after the data it checks and that nothing validates the `package_unit` column today (#70). `openapi.yaml` constrains `package_unit` to g/ml/pcs/null on input, so a row outside that set reached the catalog some other way — a migration, a seed, or a hand edit.
diagnosis.which_row: Not determined, and not determinable from telemetry. The exception message names the ingredient and is withheld by design; no span, metric or log line carries an ingredient, module, plan or target value. F2 forbids me from looking. This is ASK-2, the expected ending for this failure mode.
diagnosis.is_it_the_release: No release boundary is visible, so the runbook's step-4 rollback is not indicated. `service_version=dev` served 200s on this route from 15:47 through 16:49 and 500s from 16:24 onward — the same version label on both sides of the failure. The label is `dev` because `RATION_VERSION` is empty and config.py:75 falls back; in `development` that is expected rather than a deploy problem. The runbook's other test points the same way: failures appear under two different version labels (`test-release` earlier, `dev` now), which it reads as data or a dependency rather than the deploy.
diagnosis.blast_radius: Only this route is failing. Live series in Prometheus: /api/plans 200, /health 200, /api/auth/login 204, and /api/plans/{plan_id}/shopping-list 500 only. GET /api/plans/{plan_id}/prep-plan has no metric series at all, so telemetry cannot say whether the shared catalog breaks it too; the runbook says it does and that it has no alert.
diagnosis.user_impact: The follower opening the shopping list gets a 500. There is no cached copy and no offline mode (PRD §7), so for them the system is down. Since the last process restart at ~16:49 there is no 200 on this route at all.

recommended.action: run runbook step 5 against the database and fix the catalog row whose package_unit is outside g/ml/pcs
recommended.approver: the person on call, who owns the catalog data
recommended.why: F2 forbids me from reading plan, profile, catalog or feedback rows, and F1 forbids writing to any database. The exception message, which names the row, is withheld from telemetry by design. This is the step that actually ends the incident and it is a human one.
recommended.how: docker compose -f observability/compose.yaml exec -T db psql -U ration -d ration -c "SELECT slug, package_unit FROM ingredients WHERE package_unit IS NOT NULL AND package_unit NOT IN ('g','ml','pcs');" then set that row to a unit the system models.

recommended.action: decide whether to turn RATION_RESOLVE_PACKAGE_UNITS off as an immediate mitigation
recommended.why: F6 forbids me changing application configuration and F4 forbids me reconfiguring a running service. I am recommending the decision rather than the change because it is a real trade-off and not mine: turning the flag off restores 200s on the shopping list within one restart, and it does so by skipping the check that is catching an unconvertible unit — the list would then be built from a catalog the engine cannot fully interpret, which is the kind of quietly-wrong output units.py exists to prevent. Fixing the row is the better order if the follower is not mid-shop.

recommended.action: hold the rollback that runbook step 4 would otherwise call for
recommended.why: F3 is not mine in any case, and here the telemetry does not support it: service_version `dev` served both the healthy and the failing traffic, so there is no release boundary, and the 5xx appear under two different version labels. Rolling back would move the flag's default back to false, which is the same mitigation as the entry above with more blast radius.
